newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Oct 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Oct 14.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A majority of respondents to a poll think the Interior Ministry will probably not be able to prevent vote-buying in the November 17 election. The Internet poll showed most respondents think the Democrats are best suited to form next government. The poll was conducted among 2,051 residents of Bangkok and the provinces from October 7-11. (BANGKOK POST)

- Thai prostitutes have now found their way into cyberspace. Police say the Internet has been used to promote sex services, with prospective customers encouraged to contact service girls from specific advertisements which give detailed information about the girls and their contact numbers. (THE NATION)

- The Interior Ministry is planning to open three more checkpoints along the Thai-Cambodian border to allow three Thai firms to haul logs from Cambodia. Once approved there will be 10 checkpoints opened to facilitate Thai companies to retrieve timber from Cambodia. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Securities and Exchange Commission has began a study on the margin loan system in the wake of securities companies' concerns over risks caused by the continued plunge in the equity market. A study will be conducted to find ways to control the risks caused by loans to securities companies. (KRUNG THEP THURAKIJ)

- Thai Airways International will sell its cargo business to a joint venture with private firms, led by Commercial Transport International Co, which will hold a 26 percent stake in the venture. The sale is subject to cabinet approval of a proposal by the Civil Aviation Board to establish a national air cargo company, but it runs counter to an earlier cabinet resolution in which the airline is supposed to hold only 25 percent of the new venture and continue its existing cargo business separately. (THE NATION)
